# CSS/Stylo continuation roadmap

Fix 142 restores random indices when speculative CSS parsing fails, including registered syntax alternatives, typed math finalizers and the enclosing grid shorthand. The final installed browser passes all 46 targeted WPT assertions; 507 regression signatures and seven harness endings remain unchanged. The paired run repairs 18 failures. The standalone payload contains four Rust files and two WPT pages. After its verified signed commit, the branch has 141 accepted fixes and 142 tracked fixes, with held fix 120 excluded. The seven-claim Lean witness is conditional and post-discovery; canonical CSS-library coverage is unchanged.

Next: review consumer contracts for the release-confirmed finite ModRem/Round zero-basis candidate, then perform configured typechecking and paired browser validation if those obligations hold. Continue provider readiness and SCC work, registered-initial retention, and contextual easing lifecycle validation. Preserve the accepted random-counter and line-height changes in all future experimental restoration. The bounded enclosing-parser audit found no additional observable witness; do not count internal discarded state as another browser bug. Bloom milestones 1–6 remain complete within their documented profiles and assumptions; broader CSS/native refinement remains open. Keep research preceding each standalone native fix and its necessary WPT, and keep all work local.

Untracked audit: all 70 project files were accounted for before committing the two landing WPTs. The remaining 68 project files are held prototypes and tests; 495 unrelated paths were left untouched and their contents were not inspected. Preserve the committed recovery inventory.

Earlier roadmap checkpoints follow as history; unresolved obligations remain in scope.

# CSS/Stylo continuation roadmap

Fix 141 resolves contextual leaves in unitless line-height. The final installed browser passes all 34 WPT subtests, repairing seven original failures; 22 regression signatures and six harness endings remain unchanged. The standalone payload contains one Rust file and two WPT pages. After its verified signed commit, the branch has 140 accepted fixes and 141 tracked fixes, with held fix 120 excluded from acceptance. The accompanying Lean model is conditional and post-discovery; canonical CSS-library coverage is unchanged.

Next: typecheck corrected random-counter source v4, then run its 46 targeted WPT subtests against an authenticated original. Preserve the accepted line-height, zoom and page-selector fixes when rebasing experiments. Continue provider readiness/SCC work and the remaining Bloom/CSS verification milestones; provider work and held fix 120 remain unaccepted. Keep each future native fix with its necessary WPT in a standalone commit, with research preceding it. All work stays local.

Earlier roadmap checkpoints are retained below as history; their unresolved work remains in scope.


Fix 140 is committed as `c13f212eb28476eb31940f62299c4b4a3ae8750e` after verification research `e4ba214e3286b7a2307795c2c1f72c07706a528d`. Page-selector matching and specificity now use the matching name and pseudo-classes on the same selector. The paired 24-print-test run changes 10 failures to passes and preserves 14 passing controls/regressions. The standalone commit contains two Rust files and three WPT/reference pairs. Six scoped Lean claims and two false controls support the bucket-filtering argument; no native-refinement or canonical CSS coverage increment is claimed. Accepted fixes: 139; tracked: 140; held fix 120 remains excluded.

1. Next browser investigation: registered random syntax backtracking. The sealed v2 probe has 15 cases and 45 snapshots, including literal-initial ordinary declarations. Run against the local Nightly with support checks. Failed alternatives consume a counter outside cssparser rollback in the source; browser confirmation and any repair remain pending. Simple reparsing does not establish random-key churn.
2. Provider readiness: v5 prototype repairs pending invalidated-SCC raw-value visibility found in v4. Its finite witness rejects raw and missing-value false controls. V5 still needs configured native typechecking; production context certification, complete traversal suspension and conservative line-height scheduling remain incomplete. The live partial provider-v5 experiment is a different older prototype and stays unaccepted.
3. Registered initial retention passed configured Rust checking but needs linked-browser preservation tests and full selected-value independence validation. Its stylist base must be rebased over accepted page fix140 before installation.
4. Contextual easing dependency handoff passed Gecko Rust checking; Servo-only paths and six lifecycle WPTs remain unexecuted. CSSWG element-dependent easing policy remains unresolved. Keep generic Sign/Atan2 activation held until consumer contracts are satisfied.
5. Relative finite ModRem/Round zero-basis folding is release-confirmed with nine discrepancies and 45 matching targets. The held two-guard proposal, five-claim witness and 18-WPT proposal still need consumer review, native compilation and paired browser validation.
6. Continue Bloom milestones1–6 and broader CSS-to-implementation verification alongside observable bug discovery. Models, static source reviews and browser comparisons remain distinct evidence. Preserve accepted fixes when restoring prototypes; old source snapshots and rollback recipes require rebasing over fix140. Keep all work local.

ledger_entry.formal_attribution: Seven scoped kernel-checked outer-rollback claims and three rejected false controls explain why successful typed parses require an enclosing transaction when the surrounding grammar rejects. Post-discovery, conditional model; no Rust refinement, PRNG, floating-point or exhaustive parser proof.
